horses that have run in or completed no more than two Flat Races;

horses that have run in and completed three Flat Races and have not been placed in the first four in any of those Races;

horses that have won a Flat Race;

horses that have the highest Handicap Rating for Flat Races;

horses with the fewest unplaced runs in Flat Races.

Where horses have identical performances or Handicap Ratings, horses previously eliminated during the current year from a Flat Race run under these Rules that is not a Handicap Race shall be protected from elimination first, and priority shall be given to the horse with the greatest number of such eliminations.

National Hunt Flat Races

Protection from elimination in National Hunt Flat Races, other than Intermediate or Maiden National Hunt Flat Races, Pattern Races and Listed Races, shall operate in the following order of priority, subject to paragraph 34 (Category 1 Elimination):

horses that have been placed in the first four in a National Hunt Flat Race;

horses that have not run in a National Hunt Flat Race;

horses that have run in no more than one National Hunt Flat Race;.

horses that have run in no more than two National Hunt Flat Races.

Protection from elimination in Intermediate National Hunt Flat Races (Category 2 Elimination), other than Pattern Races and Listed Races, shall operate in the following order of priority, subject to paragraph 34:

horses that have been placed in the first four in a National Hunt Flat Race;

horses that have run in no more than one National Hunt Flat Race;

horses that have not run in a National Hunt Flat Race;

horses that have run in no more than two National Hunt Flat Races.

Protection from elimination in Maiden National Hunt Flat Races, other than Pattern Races and Listed Races, shall operate in the following order, subject to paragraph 34 (Category 3 Elimination):

horses that have been placed second, third or fourth in a National Hunt Flat Race;

horses that have run in exactly two National Hunt Flat Races;

horses that have run in exactly one National Hunt Flat Race;.

horses that have not run in a National Hunt Flat Race.

Where horses have identical performances or Handicap Ratings, horses previously eliminated at any time from a National Hunt Flat Race run under these Rules shall be protected from elimination first, and priority shall be given to the horse with the greatest number of such eliminations.

Hurdle Races, other than Handicap Hurdle Races, Maiden Races, Pattern Races, Listed Raced and Classified Stakes Races

Protection from elimination in Hurdle Races, other than Handicap Hurdle Races, Maiden Races, Pattern Races, Listed Races and Classified Stakes Races, shall operate in the following order, subject to paragraphs 36 and 37:

horses that have won a Hurdle Race on or after 1 January of the previous year;

horses that have run in no more than two Hurdle Races, and have been placed second, third or fourth at least once in those Races;

horses that have not run in a Hurdle Race;

horses that have run in no more than two Hurdle Races;

horses that have the highest Handicap Rating for Hurdle Races;

horses with the fewest unplaced runs in Hurdle Races.

Unplaced runs outside Great Britain and Ireland shall be disregarded when determining a horse's protection from elimination once such a horse has been placed second, third or fourth in Great Britain or Ireland and has not received a Handicap Rating for Hurdle Races.

Where horses have identical performances or Handicap Ratings, horses previously eliminated during the current season from a Hurdle Race run under these Rules that is not a Handicap Race shall be protected from elimination first, and priority shall be given to the horse with the greatest number of such eliminations.

Maiden Hurdle Races

Protection from elimination in Maiden Hurdle Races shall operate as follows:

horses that have been placed second, third or fourth in a Hurdle Race;

horses that have run at least three times and for which a Handicapper has declined to allot a Handicap Rating;

horses that have not run in a Hurdle Race;

horses that have run in no more than two Hurdle Races;

horses that have the highest Handicap Rating for Hurdle Races;

horses that have the fewest unplaced runs in Hurdle Races.

Where horses have identical performances or Handicap Ratings, horses previously eliminated at any time from a Hurdle Race run under these Rules that is not a Handicap Race shall be protected from elimination first, and priority shall be given to the horse with the greatest number of such eliminations.

Steeple Chases, other than Handicap Steeple Chases, Pattern Races, Listed Races, Classified Stakes Races and Hunters’ Steeple Chases

Protection from elimination in Steeple Chases, other than Handicap Races, Pattern Races, Listed Races, Classified Stakes Races and Hunters' Steeple Chases, shall operate as follows, subject to paragraphs 41 and 42:

horses that have won a Steeple Chase on or after 1 January of the previous year;

horses that have run in no more than two Steeple Chases and been placed second, third or fourth at least once in those Races;

horses that have not run in a Steeple Chase;

horses that have run in no more than two Steeple Chases;

horses that have the highest Handicap Rating for Steeple Chases;

horses with the fewest unplaced runs in Steeple Chases.

Unplaced runs outside Great Britain and Ireland shall be disregarded when determining a horse's protection from elimination once such a horse has been placed second, third or fourth in Great Britain or Ireland and has not received a Handicap Rating for Steeple Chases.

Where horses have identical performances or Handicap Ratings, horses previously eliminated during the current season from a Steeple Chase run under these Rules that is not a Handicap Race shall be protected from elimination first, and priority shall be given to the horse with the greatest number of such eliminations.

Class 3, 4 and 5 Novice Handicap Steeple Chases

Protection from elimination in Class 3, 4 and 5 Novice Handicap Steeple Chases shall operate as follows:

horses that have not run in a Steeple Chase if, on the initial publication of the weights, they have been allotted a weight no lower than the minimum weight for that Race.

Hunters’ Steeple Chases

Protection from elimination in Hunters’ Steeple Chases, other than Handicap Races or where stated in the Race Conditions, shall operate as follows:

horses that have won a Steeple Chase on or after 1 January of the previous year. Priority shall be given to horses with the highest Steeple Chase Handicap Rating;

horses that have been placed second, third or fourth in a Steeple Chase on or after 1 January of the previous year;

horses that have won an open Point-to-Point Steeple Chase (gentlemen’s, ladies’ or mixed open Races) in Great Britain on or after 1 January of the previous year;

horses that have won any other Point-to-Point Steeple Chase in Great Britain on or after 1 January of the previous year;

horses previously eliminated from a Steeple Chase, other than a Handicap Steeple Chase, run under these Rules during the current season;

horses with the fewest unplaced runs in Steeple Chases.

sections.title: Setting Field Size Limits

nested.html: Where necessary, Field Size Limits shall be set as follows:

for Class 1 Pattern and Listed Races, Heritage Handicaps (and
any associated consolation Races) and any other Race where it is specified in
the Race Conditions, the Field Size Limit shall be the Safety Factor or Maximum
Figure, whichever is the lower;

for Class 4, 5 or 6 Hunters'
Steeple Chases, the Field Size Limit shall be nine horses;

for any
other Race, the Field Size Limit shall be the balance of the Stabling Capacity
split between the remaining Races.
For the purposes of paragraph 45, any Race that has potential to divide shall be treated as if the division is confirmed and included in the calculation of Field Size Limits on that basis.
The BHA shall reassess Field Size Limits and adjust them if necessary:

after Closing, or after
Confirmation of Entries for Early Closers; and

after the deadline for
Declarations to Run.

sections.title: Weighing In

nested.html: After dismounting, a Jockey must remove and keep their saddle and present themselves to the Clerk of the Scales with the saddle to be weighed in.
If a Jockey is unable to remove the saddle or carry it to the weighing room, a Trainer may do so, provided that it is handed back to the Jockey unchanged before weighing in.
When weighing in, Jockeys must:

be wearing the same clothes and equipment that they wore when weighing
out; and

put onto the scales everything that was on the scales
when weighing out, except for any Excluded Equipment.
All weights shall be rounded down to the nearest whole 1lb unit.
A Jockey’s weight at weighing in must not be:
more than 1lb less than their weight at weighing out; or
2lb or more heavier than their Declared Weight at weighing out.

13A  The Stewards shall sanction the Jockey or Trainer, or both of them, when a breach of Rule (G)13.1 or 13.2 has occurred, unless the reason for the breach can be explained to the satisfaction of the Stewards.
13B  The Jockey and Trainer will both be sanctioned for a breach of (G)13.1 if no cause is established.
The Stewards may authorise the announcement of ‘Weighed In’ once:
the weighing in process has completed;

the Judge has confirmed the placings;
and
any Objections have been determined.
A Jockey must remain in the vicinity of the weighing room for five minutes after the ‘Weighed In’ announcement.
A Jockey who has failed to complete the course must report that fact to the Clerk of the Scales.

sections.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance

nested.html: Jockeys and Trainers must without delay make a Post Race Report if applicable.
A Post Race Report must be made as soon as possible to:

a Steward, or where a Steward is not
available,
a Veterinary Officer; or
the Clerk of the Scales.

The obligation on a Trainer to make a Post Race Report applies at any time after the Race, including after the horse has left the Racecourse. Once the horse has left the Racecourse, the Post Race Report must be made without delay to the BHA.
A Jockey may make a Post Race Report on behalf of a Trainer. In such circumstances, the Trainer remains responsible for ensuring that the Post Race Report is made.
If a horse loses its tongue strap during a Race, the Trainer must report this to a Steward.
A Post Race Report may be published by the BHA.

sections.title: Determining the result

nested.html:
The winner and the remaining placings in a Race shall
be determined by the order in which the leading point of each horse’s head
(excluding the ears and tongue) crosses the finish line.
Subject to subsequent correction or appeal, the result and the placings shall be determined:
by the Judge; or
if the Judge is unable to do so, by the Stewards.
A Race shall be void if the Judge or the Stewards are unable to determine the result.
If a horse is disqualified or has its placing altered, other than as a result of analysis of a stored sample, the placings of the other horses in the Race shall be altered accordingly.

sections.title: VOID ENTRIES

nested.html: An Entry shall be void if:
the horse does not have a relevant current qualifying Handicap Rating published in the latest ratings lists and:
the Handicap Rating subsequently awarded by the Handicapper makes the horse ineligible for the Race; or
the Handicapper declines to allot a Handicap Rating to the horse; or

An Entry shall not be made void on the death of the Person in whose name it was made, all rights, privileges, and liabilities that could have attached to the deceased Person if he or she had been alive shall attach to their personal representative.

sections.title: Race Entries

nested.html: <u>Minimum requirements for Race Entries</u>
Requirements as to running of the horse
A horse must:
satisfy the Race Conditions;
be qualified for the Race;
In the case of a BHA Authorised Day of Race Surface Transfer , a horse must be qualified for the Race originally published on the Racing Administration site.
not be the subject of a Non-Racing Agreement;
not be in the ownership, part-ownership or under the care or management of a Disqualified Person;

not have run at an
Unrecognised Meeting; and
satisfy any other requirement of these Rules that relate to the eligibility of a horse to be entered in a Race; and
A horse, and its sire and dam, must each be the product of a Natural Service or Covering and the horse must have had a full natural gestation in the body of the mare in which it was conceived.
If a horse has been suspended following a breach of Rule (F)37, the horse may not run in a Class 1 or 2 Flat Race Handicap until it has run in a Flat Race which is not a Class 1 or 2 Handicap.
An Entry may only be submitted for a horse trained in Great Britain if

the horse is registered in accordance with the Horse Naming Code or, if foaled outside of Great Britain, Ireland or the Channel Islands, has a name that is registered by the Recognised Racing Authority in the country of foaling;
the Owner is registered with the BHA; and

the horse has been implanted with an identifying microchip by a
Veterinary Surgeon.

sections.title: Non-runners after Declarations to Run

nested.html: If a Trainer is not going to run a horse in a Race for which it is Declared to Run, the Trainer must immediately submit a Non-Runner Notice:

if the horse is on the
Racecourse, and the Clerk of the Scales is present, to the Clerk of the Scales; or

at any other
time, to the Racing Calendar Office through the Racing Administration Website or by telephone.
A Non-Runner Notice:

must state the reason(s) why
the horse is a non-runner; and
cannot be withdrawn.
A horse for which a Non-Runner Notice is submitted shall not be permitted to run in the Race.
Self-certification
A Trainer may choose ‘self-certification’ as a reason for submitting a Non-Runner Notice. If they do:

the horse
will be immediately suspended from running in Great Britain for 7 days beginning on the day of the Race
in which it was a non-runner; and

no Disciplinary Action shall
be taken against the Trainer or Owner.
A Trainer cannot choose ‘self-certification’:
Deleted

if the reason for not running
is related to the Race’s prize money.
A Trainer’s ability to self-certify may be suspended if the Trainer’s rate of non-runners is above the relevant threshold published by the BHA.
<u>Veterinary certification</u>
A Trainer may choose unfit to run as a reason for submitting a Non-Runner Notice. If they do:

the horse
will be immediately suspended from running in Great Britain for 3 days beginning on the day of
the Race in which it was a non-runner; and

no disciplinary action shall be taken against the Trainer or Owner if an
acceptable veterinary certificate is received by the BHA within 7 days of the Race.
A horse may be certified unfit to run:

at the Racecourse, by a
Veterinary Officer; or

at any other
time, by a Veterinary Surgeon who is independent of the Owner, Trainer and any
Person shown in the Stable Employee Register as
employed by the Trainer.
Veterinary certificates must be signed by the Veterinary Surgeon or Veterinary Officer who examined the horse and must state:

the date, time and place of
the veterinary examination;

the meeting and date for
which the horse has been declared to run; and

the abnormal clinical findings which make reason why the horse is
unfit to run.
<u>Going</u>
A Trainer may choose ‘going’ as a reason for submitting a Non-Runner Notice. If they do, disciplinary action shall be taken unless:

the going is different from
the going on the day the horse was declared to run; or

the horse is
on the Racecourse, its identity has been verified by a Veterinary Officer and
the Trainer considers the horse will be unsuited by the going.
<u>Other</u>

A Trainer may use any other reason for submitting a Non-Runner Notice. If they do, disciplinary action shall be taken unless the BHA is satisfied that the horse’s failure to run was caused by circumstances outside of the Trainer or Owner’s control.

sections.title: Substitution of Jockeys

nested.html: A Jockey may not be substituted for another Jockey after the deadline for Declaration of Jockeys, unless:

the BHA are satisfied that the substitute Jockey can be weighed out for
the Race and:

the declared Jockey is ill or unfit to
ride;
the declared Jockey is not qualified to ride;

a meeting on the same day has been abandoned and the
substitute Jockey was declared to ride at the abandoned meeting;

the substitute Jockey was declared to ride at another
meeting on the same day and one of their declared rides is a non-runner;

the substitute Jockey was declared to ride another
horse in the same race but the horse is a non-runner;

the substitute Jockey was not declared to ride because
he had already been declared to ride at nine meetings in the week but
subsequently did not ride at one or more of those meetings; or
the declared Jockey is due to carry 1lb or more overweight, or
the BHA otherwise consents
If a Jockey is prevented from weighing out because they are 4lbs or more overweight:

if the declared Jockey was entitled to claim a weight
allowance, the substitute Jockey must also be entitled to claim a weight
allowance; or

if the declared Jockey was not entitled to claim a
weight allowance, the substitute Jockey must also not be entitled to claim a
weight allowance,
except in Races confined to:
Apprentice Jockeys;
Conditional Jockeys;
Amateur Jockeys; or,

both Conditional Jockeys and Amateur
Jockeys.
A Trainer must submit any request to substitute a Jockey as soon as possible:
to the Racing Calendar Office, or
if the Trainer is at the Racecourse, to the Stewards.

sections.title: Horses

nested.html: The Stewards may:
direct that any horse be examined;
direct that a Sample is taken from any horse for analysis;

direct that a horse stays in the Racecourse Stables
for examination for up to 24 hours after the Race in which it was declared to run;
withdraw a horse from a Race:
if they are not satisfied that it is qualified for that Race;
where there are welfare concerns;
where any person prevents or seeks to prevent access to the horse;
if it is unruly;
if it may delay the start of the Race;

where the Jockey is not in control of the horse on the way to the
start; or

where there has been a breach of the
Rules.
The Stewards will disqualify a horse where:

the Jockey causes interference which is Dangerous
Riding;
the Jockey remounts and continues in the Race;
subject to Rule (G)13, the horse did not carry at least the correct weight throughout the Race;

the horse was led over a hurdle or steeple chase
fence; or
the Jockey re-joins the Race having pulled up for any reason listed within Rule (F)26.
The Stewards may disqualify a horse where:
the horse did not cover the correct course; or
the Jockey did not present themselves to be weighed in.

The Stewards will, where a horse or Jockey causes interference, which is not Dangerous Riding, and the Stewards are satisfied that the interference improved the placing of the horse in relation to the horse or horses with which it interfered, place the horse that caused the interference behind the horse or horses with which it has interfered.

sections.html:
The Stewards may:

direct that any horse be examined;

direct that a Sample is taken from any horse for analysis;

direct that a horse stays in the Racecourse Stables for examination for up to 24 hours after the Race in which it was declared to run;

withdraw a horse from a Race:

if they are not satisfied that it is qualified for that Race;

where there are welfare concerns;

where any person prevents or seeks to prevent access to the horse;

if it is unruly;

if it may delay the start of the Race;

where the Jockey is not in control of the horse on the way to the start; or

where there has been a breach of the Rules.

The Stewards will disqualify a horse where:

the Jockey causes interference which is Dangerous Riding; 

the Jockey remounts and continues in the Race;

subject to Rule (G)13, the horse did not carry at least the correct weight throughout the Race;

the horse was led over a hurdle or steeple chase fence; or

the Jockey re-joins the Race having pulled up for any reason listed within Rule (F)26.

The Stewards may disqualify a horse where:

the horse did not cover the correct course; or

the Jockey did not present themselves to be weighed in.

The Stewards will, where a horse or Jockey causes interference, which is not Dangerous Riding, and the Stewards are satisfied that the interference improved the placing of the horse in relation to the horse or horses with which it interfered, place the horse that caused the interference behind the horse or horses with which it has interfered.

sections.title: Objections made to the Stewards

nested.html:
An Objection made to the Stewards must be brought to
their attention as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event before the
announcement of ‘Weighed In’.
The Stewards shall hold a Stewards Enquiry if:
a valid Objection is made to them; or
they believe that there are grounds for an Objection.
A Qualified Person may review a replay of the Race before making an Objection. If they do so, they must notify the Stewards and the Clerk of the Scales of the review and any subsequent Objection.
A Qualified Person must not:
raise an Objection without reasonable grounds for doing so; or
withdraw an Objection without the permission of the Stewards.
The Stewards may announce or publish details of an Objection.

27A   A riding suspension imposed on a Jockey by the Whip Review Committee will start the later of:
27A.1 14 days after the date of the written decision of the Whip Review Committee; or
27A.2 the day after an appeal of the Whip Review Committee’s decision has been determined; or
27A.3 the day after an existing suspension ends.

27B   If accepting a penalty from the Whip Review Committee, a Jockey may request that any suspension is issued in accordance with the timeline outlined in Rule (H)27, providing that the request is made before the deadline for Jockey Declarations for the first Race affected by the change.
Days on which a riding suspension shall apply
A period of suspension may:
apply only to days:
on which Flat Races are programmed to take place, if the Jockey is licensed to ride in Flat Races;
on which Jump Races are programmed to take place, if the Jockey is licensed to ride in Jump Races; or
as determined by the Stewards, if the Jockey is licensed to ride in both Flat and Jump Races or is an Amateur Jockey; and
include any day on which a Jockey is required to attend remedial training.
The days on which a suspension applies shall not change if any meetings are subsequently moved or abandoned, unless otherwise directed by the BHA.

sections.title: Health requirements

nested.html: A horse must not have been tubed (tracheostomy), unless the tubing took place before 1 October 2012, and the Trainer of the horse produces a certificate, signed by a Veterinary Surgeon, that confirms the date of tubing. A tubed horse must:
not run in a Race on an All Weather Track;
not run in a Race wearing a martingale; and
have the plug in the tube removed before a Race.
A horse must not have any implant, unless the implant is:
pharmacologically inactive; or
a suprachoroidal cyclosporine implant for the treatment of immune mediated corneal disease or autoimmune uveitis that has previously been approved by the BHA.
A horse must not have received anything other than normal feed and water in contravention of Rule (D)11.1.
A horse must:
be vaccinated in accordance with the Vaccinations Code; and,
not have been given any vaccination on Race day or on any of the six clear days before.
A horse must not have been administered with:
any intra-articular injection of any substance on Race day or on any of the 14 clear days before;
any bisphosphonate*:
before the horse is aged four years (as of 01 January of the horse’s year of birth):
on Race day or any of the 30 clear days before;
extracorporeal shockwave therapy on the day of the Race or any of the 5 clear days before.
any beta-2 agonist** on Race day or on any of the clear 30 days before
*See BHA Notice: Bisphosphonates here
** See BHA Notice: beta-2 agonists here
A horse must not have undergone:
a neurectomy, or
a laparoscopic sterilisation on or after 1 April 2010, unless:
the horse is a mare or filly and a satisfactory veterinary certificate is submitted to The Racing Calendar Office which confirms that she has undergone the procedure for therapeutic reasons; or
the horse is subsequently gelded.
A horse must not have received a blood transfusion for the purpose of enhancing its performance in the Race.
A horse must not be more than 120 days pregnant.
A horse must not have had its heritable genome modified.

sections.title: Training Requirements

nested.html: Except for Hunters’ Steeple Chases, the Grand Military Gold Cup and the Royal Artillery Gold Cup, before a horse can run in a Race it must have been in the care of and trained by:
a Trainer with a Licence to train horses for the Race in question; or
the equivalent from another Recognised Racing Authority;
for the day of the Race and the 14 clear days before the Race.

Once it has run in a Hunters’ Steeple Chase, unless the horse is under the care of a Permit Trainer a horse may not run in any Steeple Chase other than a Hunters’ Steeple Chase, the Grand Military Gold Cup and the Royal Artillery Gold Cup, during that same Hunters’ Steeple Chase Season.
A horse must not, on the day of the Race or any of the 14 clear days before, have visited an equine swimming pool in Great Britain that has not been Licensed by the BHA .
15A A horse may not run in a National Hunt Flat Race if it has previously run in a total of three National Hunt Flat Races, Irish National Hunt Flat races, and/or French AQPS races, except;
15A.1 a horse may run in a fourth National Hunt Flat Race if any of its first three runs were in a Pattern or Listed Race or its fourth run is to be in a Pattern or Listed Race
15A.2 a horse may run in a fifth National Hunt Flat Race if its fifth run is a Pattern Race held during the same season as its fourth run.

sections.title: Additional Requirements for Hunters’ Steeple Chases

nested.html: A horse must have a Hunter Certificate to run in a Hunters’ Steeple Chase.

A horse cannot run in a Hunters’ Steeple Chase if, at any time on or after 1 November in the year before the Race, the horse was in the care of a Permit Trainer who was not permitted to train horses for the Owner of the horse in question at the time when the horse was in their care.

A horse cannot run in a Hunters’ Steeple Chase if, in
the 15 months prior to the beginning of the Hunters’ Steeple Chase Season and/or during the current Hunters’ Steeple Chase Season it
has:

been placed first, second or third in a Grade 1 or
Grade 2 Steeple Chase in Great Britain or Ireland, or equivalent overseas Race.
After a Hunter Certificate has been registered for a horse, the horse may be entered into any Hunter’s Steeple Chase for which it is eligible subject to the following:
if the Hunter Certificate was registered before 12pm, the horse may not enter any Hunter’s Steeple Chase that is Closing on the same day the horse was registered;
if the Hunter Certificate was registered after 12pm, the horse may not enter any Hunter’s Steeple Chase that is Closing on the same day or day after the horse was registered.

sections.title: Additional requirements for horses trained outside Great Britain

nested.html: A horse foaled or trained outside Great Britain cannot run in a Race if it has been in Great Britain for more than 90 days starting from:
the date the Racing Clearance Notification was issued;
the date the horse's Passport was endorsed by the Recognised Racing Authority of the country where the horse is trained; or
the date a horse trained in Ireland arrived in Great Britain.
Paragraph 20 does not apply if the horse is in the care of:
a Trainer;
a trainer licensed by a Recognised Racing Authority with permission from the BHA.
A horse that has been in Great Britain for a period of 90 days or less must at all times be supervised by the trainer.
Unless otherwise directed by the BHA, a horse trained outside Great Britain must have had a Sample taken by the BHA.

sections.title: Handicapping

nested.html: No horse may run in a Race unless they meet the previous experience requirements in the Weights and Handicapping Code for the classification of that Race.
A horse shall be eligible to receive a Handicap Rating in accordance with the Weights and Handicapping Code.
The BHA may refuse to give a Handicap Rating to any horse if, in the BHA’s opinion, it does not have sufficient information to do so.
A Handicap Rating which is published on Tuesday of a particular week shall, unless the BHA directs otherwise, apply for Races that Close on that Tuesday through to the following Monday.
A weight may not be altered after it has been published, unless before the relevant deadline, the BHA permits:

a weight to be added where the horse was entered for
the race but its name or weight was omitted from the Handicap; or
a correction to be made where an incorrect weight has been published.
No alteration to published weights shall be permitted:

in respect of an Early Closer, after noon on the Friday before the
first Scratching Deadline; or
otherwise, after 9am on the day that Declarations to Run are due.

sections.title: Employment and registration of persons working in stables

nested.html:
Before employing anyone, where applicable, a Trainer
must obtain a reference from the last Trainer that employed the applicant.
1A Stable Staff will be required to provide the necessary DBS certificate to their employer for review in accordance with the BHA’s published DBS policy.
A Trainer must ensure that the following persons are entered on the Stable Employee Register, by making an application to the Racing Calendar Office on the same day as the person starting:

the
Trainer’s employees (including part-time employees); and

any
persons with regular access to or involvement with the Trainer’s stable, except for:

service
providers; and

Owners,
unless they have duties in the stables.

Where a Trainer requires one of their Stable Employees
to access the Racecourse Stables, they must:
apply for a BHA Identity Card for that employee; and

keep possession of the BHA Identity Card at all times
except when it is required by the employee to access Racecourse Stables.
Where the employment of a Stable Employee ends, the Trainer must notify the Racing Calendar Office:

immediately,
if the employee is an Apprentice Jockey or a Conditional Jockey; or

otherwise,
within 8 days,
and destroy any BHA Identity Card issued to that former employee.

<u>Employment
of schoolchildren</u>
Before hiring a schoolchild, a Trainer must obtain the approval of the Local Education Authority.

agree to accept or solicit, any Consideration in connection with riding in a

a Professional Jockey may accept, agree to accept or solicit:

the provision of views or information for general publication,

where such arrangements are entered into with a Betting Operator, they must
provide to the BHA all details of the arrangement, or any changes to the
arrangement, as soon as reasonably practicable.

sections.title: Inside Information

nested.html:
No Person may communicate
Inside Information to any other person unless permitted to do so under these Rules.

Except where the Person communicating the Inside Information knows or has reason to know that the Inside Information shall be used for prohibited Betting and/or lay Betting, a Person can communicate Inside Information to a Person who owns, trains or is a service provider or Stable Employee responsible for or engaged in the care and welfare of that horse.

Inside Information public, a Person can communicate Inside Information to:
the General Public directly;

an accredited journalist for the purposes of publishing the Inside
Information to the General Public; or

at a Public Event, provided that the person
communicating the Inside Information is paid no more than a reasonable fee for
attending the event.

sections.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting

nested.html: A Trainer and their Stable Employees must not place a lay Bet on a horse under their care.
Rule (J)6 continues to apply to a Stable Employee for a period of 21 days after they leave the employment of the Trainer.
A Jockey’s Agent must not place a lay Bet on a horse being ridden by a Jockey they represent.
A Listed Person must not place a lay Bet on a horse in which they have any interest.

A Service Provider must not place a lay Bet on a horse owned, trained or ridden by a Person to whom they have provided a service, for the whole of the period in which the service was provided and for 21 days afterwards.
A lay Bet includes a match Bet.

sections.title: Conduct prejudicial to horseracing

nested.html: A Person must not engage in conduct which the BHA considers is prejudicial to the integrity, proper conduct or good reputation of horseracing in Great Britain.
19A  Persons must comply with the BHA Code of Conduct.
Individuals not bound by the Rules of Racing should be aware that the BHA Code of Conduct also applies to them.
A Person must not act in a violent or improper manner.
A Person must not abuse a BHA Official, whether verbally or otherwise.
Any Person who engages in bloodstock transactions or deals in racehorses (including horses intended for racing), must comply with the Bloodstock Industry Code of Practice (available here).
A Person must not, without the prior written permission of the BHA, associate with the following in connection with horseracing in Great Britain:
a Disqualified Person; or
a person subject to an Exclusion Order.

sections.title: Circumstances in which amounts may not be payable

nested.html:
No Stake is payable, and any
Stake paid shall be refunded, for the following:
an Entry that is void;

a horse that is not qualified
to start in a Race at the time of Closing;

a horse that is eliminated
from an over-subscribed Race;

a horse that does not run in a Race if it would be
required to carry more than 11st 12lb in a Second Preference Race;
a Race that is void; or
a Race that is not run.

The BHA may waive fees relating to a Scratching Deadline and withdraw a horse from the Race where it is satisfied that the horse was left in the Race at a Scratching Deadline due to circumstances in which it would not be reasonable to expect the Person responsible to prevent or avoid, subject to payment of an administrative fee.

sections.title: Distribution of Pool Money

nested.html: Pool Money shall be paid four times per year to the relevant Trainer, who shall distribute the sums to the current and former stable employees as entered in the Stable Employee Register in accordance with the stable’s Prize Money distribution criteria.

A stable’s Prize Money
distribution criteria shall be decided by the employees and must be displayed at the stable yard in a place where it
can be inspected by all employees.
When the Pool Money is paid to the Trainer, the BHA shall send a Stable Employee Return to the Trainer who must:
add to the Stable Employee Return:

the date on which the payment
to stable employees will be made; and

the amount to be paid to each
stable employee.
sign and return a copy of the Stable Employee Return as so amended to the BHA within 21 days of the date printed on the Stable Employee Return;

display a copy of the Stable Employee Return as so amended at the
stable in a place where it can be inspected by all employees for at least 10
days from the date the Stable Employee Return is returned to the BHA.
A Trainer:

must make the payments shown on the Stable Employee
Return not less than 10 days before, and not more than 21 days after, signing
and returning the Stable Employee Return to the BHA; and
may not deduct any amount except for income tax,
unless otherwise directed by the BHA.
A stable employee may request that a Trainer withhold payment until a later date. Following such request, the Trainer must:

take all reasonable steps to
obtain a return on the money; and

pay it to the employee
promptly if the employee leaves the Trainer's
employment.

sections.html:
Pool Money shall be paid four times per year to the relevant Trainer, who shall distribute the sums to the current and former stable employees as entered in the Stable Employee Register in accordance with the stable’s Prize Money distribution criteria.

A stable’s Prize Money distribution criteria shall be decided by the employees and must be displayed at the stable yard in a place where it can be inspected by all employees.

When the Pool Money is paid to the Trainer, the BHA shall send a Stable Employee Return to the Trainer who must:

add to the Stable Employee Return:

the name of any current or former stable employee employed during the period covered by the payment and to whom a payment is to be made;

the date on which the payment to stable employees will be made; and

the amount to be paid to each stable employee.

sign and return a copy of the Stable Employee Return as so amended to the BHA within 21 days of the date printed on the Stable Employee Return;

display a copy of the Stable Employee Return as so amended at the stable in a place where it can be inspected by all employees for at least 10 days from the date the Stable Employee Return is returned to the BHA.

A Trainer:

sections.title: B SAMPLES

nested.html: Procedure

The B Sample shall be analysed at the LGC laboratory, unless the Responsible Person nominates the Laboratorie Des Courses Hippiques (LCH) or the Deutsche Sporthochschule Koln Institut fur Biochemie (DSKIB), or another laboratory with permission from the BHA.
The Responsible Person may, at their own cost, appoint an appropriately qualified representative to witness the analysis of the B Sample, provided they are available on the designated date.

If the Responsible Person elects to have the B Sample analysed at a laboratory other than the LGC laboratory, the Responsible Person shall bear the corresponding costs. In all other cases, a Disciplinary Panel has the power to order that a contribution is made of up to £500 to the costs of the B Sample.
ANALYSIS
The analysis of the B Sample will be limited to confirming whether the B Sample confirms the findings of the A Sample.
A copy of the results and any supporting evidence shall be provided to the BHA and the Responsible Person.

sections.title: ENDOGENOUS SUBSTANCES

nested.html: If an Adverse Analytical Finding involves an endogenous substance, the BHA or the Responsible Person may elect to have further Samples taken or for further examinations of the horse to take place to investigate whether the quantity of the substance found could have been produced naturally by the horse. The costs of analysing any further Samples shall be borne equally by the BHA and Responsible Person.

If an Adverse Analytical Finding involves an endogenous substance, the BHA may carry out an investigation prior to notifying the Responsible Person of the finding, save that the BHA shall notify the Responsible Person prior to analysing the B Sample.
If samples of food or other substances are removed from the yard or premises, the Responsible Person may appoint a person to observe any analysis of the sample.
Following that analysis, the Responsible Person may arrange for their own tests to be carried out at a laboratory nominated by them. If they do so:
they must make a written request to the BHA for the samples to be released;
the testing must be carried out at an Approved Laboratory; and
if the BHA appoints an analyst to review the laboratory’s processes, the analyst must be given the option of witnessing the analysis of the sample.

sections.title: Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body

nested.html: It is not necessary to demonstrate intent, fault, negligence or knowing use to establish a breach of Rule (K)2.
There shall be no breach of Rule (K)2.2 if:
the Category B Prohibited Substance is administered for genuine therapeutic purposes; and
the horse does not run in a Race on that day; and
the BHA is notified of the administration beforehand or, if urgent, as soon as reasonably practicable.
The presence of a Prohibited Substance in the following is sufficient evidence of a breach of Rule (K)2.
the horse’s ‘A’ Sample where
(i) the B sample is not analysed; or
(ii) the B Sample is analysed and is found to be compromised;
the horse’s A and B sample;
both portions of the B Sample, where the B Sample is split into two portions as a result of the horse’s A Sample being unavailable or where it is believed to have been compromised.
The Disciplinary Panel shall impose a penalty on the Responsible Person for a breach of Rule (K)2 unless the Responsible Person establishes:
the precise route as to how the Prohibited Substance entered their horse’s body; and
that they had taken all reasonable precautions to avoid violating Rule (K)2.

(i) the B sample is not analysed; or

(ii) the B Sample is analysed and is found to be compromised;

the horse’s A and B sample;

both portions of the B Sample, where the B Sample is split into two portions as a result of the horse’s A Sample being unavailable or where it is believed to have been compromised.

The Disciplinary Panel shall impose a penalty on the Responsible Person for a breach of Rule (K)2 unless the Responsible Person establishes:

the precise route as to how the Prohibited Substance entered their horse’s body; and

that they had taken all reasonable precautions to avoid violating Rule (K)2.

sections.title: Horse Disqualifications

nested.html: A horse shall be disqualified from a Race already run if:
it has been the subject of fraudulent practice;
at the time of the Race, the Jockey was not permitted to ride under these Rules;

at the time of the Race, the horse was subject to a
suspension;
a Sample from the horse tests positive for a Prohibited Substance;
the Responsible Person does not comply with the Sample collection provisions of Chapter K;
the requirements for a horse to enter at paragraphs 12 to 20 of the Race Entry Code, and/or the qualifications for a horse to run in the Running Requirements Code have not been complied with;
it carried less than the weight that it should have carried;
it used a different name from that specified in the Register of Horse Names;
it is the subject of a lease and ran in a Selling or Claiming Race without the lessee having obtained the lessor’s prior written consent;
it was the subject of an inaccurate, misleading or fraudulent declaration at the time of registration with the Stud Book and/or the BHA; or
its Jockey has been found in breach of Rule (F)45 and the number of strikes (excluding those found to be clearly and unequivocally for safety purposes) is 4 or more above the permitted level.

A horse may be disqualified from a Race already run if an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation has been
committed.
If a horse is disqualified:
it shall not be given a position in the Race;
it is not entitled to any prize; and

except in the case of a stored Sample, the other horses’ positions
shall be adjusted accordingly.
If a horse’s position is adjusted:
it is only entitled to the prize for the adjusted position; and
the other horses’ positions shall be adjusted accordingly.

Other than in exceptional circumstances, if a horse is disqualified because it tested positive for a Prohibited Substance all prize money, other prizes or trophies must be repaid or surrendered as directed by the BHA.
If a horse is disqualified because it tested positive for a Prohibited Substance in a stored sample there shall be no alteration in the placing of any other horse in the Race.

sections.title: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order

nested.html: A Disqualified Person and anyone made the subject of an Exclusion Order may not:

except where expressly provided by the Disciplinary Panel, be employed
by a Trainer;
enter Licensed Premises;
be involved in any way with a horse that has ever been subject to these Rules, unless the BHA directs otherwise;
be a BHA Official;
be an Authorised Agent;
enter, run, train or ride a horse in any Race, subject to any grace period under Chapter B;
be associated with a Licensed equine swimming pool; or

lease, or continue to lease, any horse that he owns to
a third party, unless he has the BHA’s approval to do so.
Any horse with which a Disqualified Person, or anyone made the subject of an Exclusion Order, has any involvement:
shall be suspended from racing; and

the suspension shall remain in place until the horse
has been sold on the open market to someone who
has no connection with the Disqualified Person, or the person to whom the Exclusion Order applies, or until the expiry of
the disqualification or Exclusion Order.
A Trainer shall not train a horse owned by a Disqualified Person, or a person the subject of an Exclusion Order, without the BHA’s permission.

sections.title: Action taken by the BHA

nested.html: <u>Exclusion Order</u>

The BHA may issue an Exclusion Order against any person, whether or not they are subject to the Rules, where it is in the interests of racing to do so. The Exclusion Order may be indefinite, or for such period as the BHA may specify.
Power to prohibit Overseas Jockeys from riding in Races
The BHA may prohibit an Overseas Jockey from taking part in Race(s) for such period as it considers appropriate.
An Overseas Jockey may appeal the prohibition to a Disciplinary Panel in accordance with the Judicial Panels Code.
Suspension

Any suspension imposed under the Regulations for
Point-to-Point Steeple Chases or the Regulations for Arabian Horse Racing will
also have effect under these Rules.
Horse Suspension Grounds
The BHA may suspend a horse in the following circumstances:
Ground 1: a horse has been the subject of fraudulent practice;
Ground 2: a Sample collected from a horse tested positive under Chapter K;
Ground 3: a horse is the subject of an inaccurate, misleading or fraudulent declaration at the time of registration with the Stud Book Authority or the BHA;
Ground 4: there is a reasonable suspicion that an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation has been committed;
Ground 5: the horse’s previous performances suggest the horse may be a risk to itself, to another horse or to a Jockey;
Ground 6: there are other welfare concerns;
Ground 7: there has been a failure to pay for the horse in accordance with the Claiming and Selling Code; or
Ground 8: any other circumstances where it would be appropriate to do so.
Where a suspension is issued on the basis of one or more of the Horse Suspension Grounds, the Trainer, Jockey or Owner of the horse may apply to the Disciplinary Panel to lift the suspension.
The Disciplinary Panel shall only lift the suspension where the Trainer, Jockey or Owner of the horse has established good reason for reinstatement.
Where a horse is suspended in accordance with Ground 5 of the Horse Suspension Grounds, any reinstatement may be subject to such conditions as may be set by the BHA.
Performance-related suspensions
Any horse suspended due to concerns with its jumping ability shall be required to pass a jumping assessment before its suspension is lifted.
A horse suspended from running three times due to its performance shall be suspended from running, or running in specific types of race, indefinitely
Jockey Suspensions
The BHA may suspend the licence of any Jockey that has returned a Positive Analysis until the conclusion of any Disciplinary Panel proceedings.
The Jockey may apply to the Licensing Committee to lift a suspension impose under Rule (L)23.
The Licensing Committee shall only lift the suspension where the Jockey has established good reason for reinstatement.
Racecourses
Once a Racecourse Licence has been granted, the BHA may issue fixed penalty notices up to a maximum amount of £500 in respect of a failure to comply with a requirement imposed by these Rules.

sections.title: Disciplinary Panels

nested.html: The BHA has the power to take disciplinary action where it considers that there is reason to believe that there has been a breach of the Rules. It shall do so in accordance with the Judicial Panels Code.
Sanction
Where a Disciplinary Panel finds that there has been a breach of these Rules, the Disciplinary Panel may do one or more of the following, in accordance with the Penalty Guidelines:
impose a caution;
impose a financial penalty not exceeding £75,000;
impose the suspension or withdrawal of a Licence;

declare that a Person is ineligible for a Licence, or
other form of registration, under these Rules for such period as it may specify;

declare that a Person is a Disqualified Person for such period as it may
specify (including indefinitely);

declare that no application to be employed in racing
stables by a Disqualified Person be made for such period as it may specify;
issue an Exclusion Order;

order a Jockey to attend a course in remedial training
at the British Racing School or National Horseracing College;

appropriate; or

A penalty, or part of it, may be deferred, suspended or be contingent

Sanction

Where a Disciplinary Panel finds that there has been a breach of these Rules, the Disciplinary Panel may do one or more of the following, in accordance with the Penalty Guidelines:

impose a caution;

impose a financial penalty not exceeding £75,000;

impose the suspension or withdrawal of a Licence;

declare that a Person is ineligible for a Licence, or other form of registration, under these Rules for such period as it may specify;

declare that a Person is a Disqualified Person for such period as it may specify (including indefinitely);

declare that no application to be employed in racing stables by a Disqualified Person be made for such period as it may specify;

issue an Exclusion Order;

order a Jockey to attend a course in remedial training at the British Racing School or National Horseracing College;

disqualify a horse from one or more Races;

suspend a horse from running in certain Races or for such period of time as it may specify, and subject to any conditions it deems appropriate; or

such other penalty or order as it considers appropriate.

A penalty, or part of it, may be deferred, suspended or be contingent on an event.

sections.title: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons

nested.html: A Disqualified Person may apply for permission to be employed in a racing stable, but not before the later of:
the expiry of the time limit for appealing the disqualification;
any appeal of the disqualification has been determined; or
the expiry of any period set by the Disciplinary Panel before an application can be made.
An application may be heard by a different Disciplinary Panel than the one which imposed the disqualification.
An application must include:
a full written submission in support;
all evidence and documents on which the applicant wishes to rely; and
a summary of the evidence of any supporting witness.
Where an application is filed, the BHA shall be asked by the Disciplinary Panel:
whether or not it opposes the application; and
the reasons for any opposition.

After the BHA’s response has been filed, the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson shall decide how to proceed to determine the application, including whether or not to hold an oral hearing. Such decision shall be final and binding.
Commencement of sanction
Unless otherwise stated, a decision of a Disciplinary Panel shall take effect on the later of the time for an appeal expiring or an appeal being finally determined.

sections.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications

nested.html: Subject to Rule (L)40, the BHA shall reciprocate a suspension or disqualification imposed by another Recognised Racing Authority unless the Recognised Racing Authority requests that it should not be reciprocal.
A Person may apply to the Disciplinary Panel for an order that the suspension or disqualification should not be reciprocated.

A Person cannot make an application for the suspension or disqualification not to be reciprocated unless they have exhausted all appeal procedures available to them under the rules of the Recognised Racing Authority.
Any application must be made in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code, and the suspension or disqualification shall be stayed pending determination.
An application must be made within three days of the later of:

the suspension or disqualification being imposed by the Recognised
Racing Authority; or

any appeal against the suspension or disqualification
under the rules of the Recognised Racing Authority being finally determined.

The Disciplinary Panel may consider an appeal brought out of time if the applicant can establish that it was not possible to do so in time and that the application was otherwise made as soon as reasonably possible.
In hearing an application, the Disciplinary Panel shall only be concerned with whether there was a failure to comply with:
the rules of the relevant Recognised Racing Authority; or

the rules of natural justice in the process that led
to the Recognised Racing Authority imposing a suspension.

Where an application is made, the relevant Recognised Racing Authority may apply to the Disciplinary Panel to be represented at any hearing. Any such application, which shall be at the Recognised Racing Authority’s own expense, shall be determined by the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson.

sections.title: Defined Percentage

nested.html:
If, at any point in a given period, a Trainer’s
Defined Percentage reaches 10%, the BHA may direct that for the remainder of
that calendar year any horse in their care that is referred for a Stalls Test
must wait for 7 days before taking a Stalls
Test.

The 7-day prohibition in paragraph 1 will not
apply to any horse that already holds an Entry for:
a Pattern Race;
a Listed Race;
a Heritage Handicap; or
an Early Closer,
when it is referred for a Stalls Test.
At the end of a calendar year:
if a Trainer’s Defined Percentage is less than 10%, the Trainer shall start the next calendar year with a Defined Percentage of zero; and
if a Trainer’s Defined Percentage is 10% or more, the Trainer will start the next calendar year with that Defined Percentage.
If, at any point in a given period, a Trainer’s Defined Percentage reaches 15%, the BHA may direct that every unraced horse in their care must take a Stalls Test before they can race.

sections.title: The Stalls Test

nested.html: The Starter may blindfold a horse for a Stalls Test.
A horse shall pass a Stalls Test if:
it is capable of being led into the stalls by one handler, with assistance from no more than four handlers at the rear; or
if the horse is loaded into the stalls with the front gate open or in reverse, it loads to the satisfaction of the Starter,
and, in either circumstance,
it remains in the stall for a minimum of one minute without becoming unruly.

sections.title: Prohibition on further Stalls Tests

nested.html:
Where a horse is prohibited from undergoing a Stalls
Test for 6 months, the Trainer may apply to the BHA for the remainder of ban to
be lifted if, during that 6 month period, the horse runs outside Great Britain
on two occasions  from starting stalls
without causing problems at the start.

fails its second consecutive attempt at a Stalls Test, it cannot take a further Stalls Test for six months; and/or
fails its third consecutive attempt at a Stalls Test, the matter shall be referred to the Disciplinary Panel.

A Jockey must not allow the horse to touch the starting tape or allow its head to be over the starting tape.

sections.title: Schooling horses for all types of start

nested.html:
A Trainer must ensure that any horse under their care is properly
schooled for all applicable types of start;
A horse shall be taken to be properly schooled for starting stalls if:
it has experience of being blindfolded;

it loads into the starting
stalls without hesitation and, if necessary, using no more than two pushers;

it is capable of standing
in starting stalls
with a horse either side for a minimum of two minutes,
and
it is capable of standing alone in the starting stalls for two minutes.

On the first occasion when a horse trained in Great
Britain runs in a Race started from starting stalls, a Trainer must inform the
Starter of any:
request for special arrangements at the start; and
specific idiosyncrasies of behaviour and / or gait.

On the first occasion when a horse trained outside
Great Britain is entered for a Race started from starting stalls, the Trainer
must provide the BHA with the relevant Recognised Racing Authority’s starter’s
view of the horse's behaviour at the start before the deadline for submitting
the Declaration to Run. If it is not provided, no special arrangements may be
made for the horse at the start.

sections.title: Trainers’ Code of Conduct in Dealings with Owners

nested.html: A Trainer must:
update the Owner about the horse’s wellbeing;

promptly inform the Owner if a horse suffers an injury and is likely to
require a prolonged period of box rest;

immediately notify the Owner if one of the Owner’s
horses ceases to be under the direct care of the Trainer and is the subject of
a separate livery charge by a third party.

If a Trainer sells a horse that they have an interest in or where they will receive a financial benefit of any kind from the sale, they must disclose that interest and/or any financial benefit they receive on the face of the invoice.
No Trainer may act for both the seller and purchaser in the sale of a horse without the consent of both parties.
A Trainer acting in the sale or purchase of a horse that they either train or are likely to train if the transaction completes must:

advise the purchaser that the horse may be examined
before purchase by a veterinary surgeon appointed by the purchaser; and
disclose:
if the horse has been seen to weave, box-walk, windsuck or crib bite;

any veterinary condition known to the Trainer which
might affect the horse’s performance; and/or
any surgery that the horse is known to have undergone.
A Trainer must:

notify the Owner before the deadline for Declarations
to Run if a horse is entered in a Claiming Race or Selling Race; and

inform and consult with the Owner whenever the Trainer
is responsible for a horse offered for sale at public auction,

unless the
Trainer has rightfully exercised an express lien, or the Owner has waived the
requirement to be notified.
Except as provided in paragraph 11, no provision of this Code may be waived by agreement between an Owner and Trainer.
Where a horse has more than one Owner, a duty under this Code to notify a seller or purchaser will be fulfilled if one Owner or their appointed representative is notified.

sections.html:
A Trainer must:

update the Owner about the horse’s wellbeing;

promptly inform the Owner if a horse suffers an injury and is likely to require a prolonged period of box rest;

immediately notify the Owner if one of the Owner’s horses ceases to be under the direct care of the Trainer and is the subject of a separate livery charge by a third party.

If a Trainer sells a horse that they have an interest in or where they will receive a financial benefit of any kind from the sale, they must disclose that interest and/or any financial benefit they receive on the face of the invoice.

No Trainer may act for both the seller and purchaser in the sale of a horse without the consent of both parties.

A Trainer acting in the sale or purchase of a horse that they either train or are likely to train if the transaction completes must:

advise the purchaser that the horse may be examined before purchase by a veterinary surgeon appointed by the purchaser; and

disclose:

if the horse has been seen to weave, box-walk, windsuck or crib bite;

any veterinary condition known to the Trainer which might affect the horse’s performance; and/or

any surgery that the horse is known to have undergone.

An Owner must pay any amount payable under a Training Agreement within

Non-payment report

include at least the following:
the Owner's name and address,
details of the debt;

the date that request for payment was
made;
be accompanied by a copy of the unpaid invoice; and
sent no later than 15 months after the sum became payable.
A Trainer must not submit an unjustified or frivolous non-payment report.
Consequences of non-payment
If an Owner cannot provide the BHA with a good explanation for late payment, they may be added to the Forfeit List.

Minimum eligibility for Handicap Rating

nested.html: A horse must have met the criteria for eligibility for a Handicap Rating by the Saturday immediately before Closing, or, if the race is an Flat Early Closer, by the Saturday immediately before publication of the weights in the Racing Calendar, or if it is a Jump Early Closer, by the Sunday immediately before publication of the weights in the Racing Calendar.
Rating Related Maiden and Novice Races and Classified Stakes Flat Races
A horse shall be eligible for a Handicap Rating for a Rating Related Maiden or Novice Race or Classified Stakes Race if:

the
horse has run in at least three Flat Races in Great Britain and/or Ireland;

the horse is trained in Great Britain and has run in
at least three Flat Races run under the rules of a Recognised Racing Authority; or
the horse is trained in Great Britain and has run in two Flat Races in Great Britain and/or Ireland having
won its first Race; or
for the purpose of running in a Class 4, 5 or 6 Rating Related Novice or Classified Stakes, has won its second Race and the Handicapper is prepared to allot a Rating of 80 or less
The horse is trained outside of Great Britain; and
has run in two Flat Races in Great Britain, having won its first Race; or

for the purpose of running in a Class 4, 5 or 6 Rating Related Novice or Classified Stakes, has run in two Flat Races in Great Britain, and having won its second Race, the Handicapper is prepared to allot a Handicap Rating of 80 or less
Deleted.

A horse shall be eligible for Handicap Rating to run in a Handicap Flat Race, other than a Nursery Handicap, with a Total Prize Fund of £45,000 or more if it is aged three or older, and:

the
horse has run at least three times in Flat Races in Great Britain;

the horse is trained in Great Britain and has run in
at least three Flat Races run under the rules of a Recognised Racing Authority; or
the horse:
is aged three or older;

is trained outside Great
Britain; and

(ii) the
horse has already run in a Handicap Flat Race in Great Britain.

the horse:
is three years old or more;
is trained in Great Britain; and
has run in:

(a) three or more Flat Races run
under the rules of a Recognised Racing Authority; or
(b) two Flat Races in Great Britain and/or Ireland, having won its first Race; or

(c) for the purpose of running in a Class 4, 5 or 6 Handicap Race, has run in two Flat Races in Great Britain and/or Ireland, and having won its second Race, the Handicapper is prepared to allot a Handicap Rating of 80 or less

the horse satisfies the

Nursery Handicaps
A horse trained in Great Britain shall be eligible for a Handicap Rating to run in a Nursery Handicap if the horse is a two-year-old and has run in:

three
or more Flat Races under the rules of any Recognised Racing Authority, with at least two of those runs being in Great Britain and/or Ireland; or
two Flat Races in Great Britain and/or Ireland, having won its first Race; or
for the purpose of running in a Class 4, 5 or 6 Nursery Handicap, has run in two Flat Races in Great Britain and/or Ireland, and either:
the horse finished in the first four places in both races; or
the horse won its second Race and the Handicapper is prepared to allot a Handicap Rating of 80 or less.
A horse trained outside Great Britain shall be eligible for a Handicap Rating to run in a Nursery Handicap if the horse is a two-year old and has run in:

three or more Flat Races in
Great Britain;

two Flat Races in Great
Britain, having won its first Race; or
for the purpose of running in a Class 4, 5 or 6 Nursery Handicap, has run in two Flat Races in Great Britain, and either:
the horse finished in the first four places in both races; or
the horse won its second Race and the Handicapper is prepared to allot a Handicap Rating of 80 or less.
Handicap Jump Races and Classified Stakes Jump Races
A horse shall be eligible for a Handicap Rating to run in a Handicap Steeple Chase, Handicap Hurdle Race, Classified Stakes Steeple Chase or Classified Stakes Hurdle Race if it has run in:

three or more Steeple Chases
and/or Hurdle Races in Great Britain, Ireland and/or France;

two Steeple Chases and/or Hurdle Races in Great
Britain, Ireland or France and finished in the first four places in both races; or
one or two Steeple Chases or Hurdle Races in Great Britain, Ireland or France and won at least one of those races, and is not a Novice or Juvenile in the type of Race entered.

Any horse that does not meet the requirements of paragraph 13 shall be eligible for a Handicap Rating to run in a Class 1, 2 or 3 Handicap Steeple Chase or Hurdle Race or Class 1, 2 or 3 classified Steeple Chase or Hurdle Race if:
the Trainer has pre-notified the Racing Calendar Office of the horse’s Entry in accordance with the Race Entry Code; and
the horse is not a Novice or Juvenile in the type of Race entered; and

the horse has run in three or more Steeple Chases
and/or Hurdle Races run under the rules of a Recognised Racing Authority.
A Novice or Juvenile shall be eligible for a Handicap Rating to run:

in a Class 1 or 2 Handicap
Steeple Chase only if:

the horse has run in three or
more Steeple Chases in Great Britain, Ireland and/or France, or

in the case of a Class 2 Handicap Steeple Chase, the
horse has run in two Steeple Chases  in
Great Britain, Ireland and/or France and finished in the first four places in
both Races;
in a Class 1 or 2 Handicap Hurdle Race not restricted to novices or juveniles, only if the horse has run in four or more Hurdle Races in Great Britain, Ireland and/or France.
in a Class 1 or 2 Handicap Hurdle Race restricted to novices or juveniles, only if the horse has run in three or more Hurdle Races in Great Britain, Ireland and/or France.

After a Scratching Deadline or Confirmation of Entries in a Handicap Flat Race that is an Early Closer, the highest original weight of the horses that remain entered in the Race shall be raised to the top weight and all other entries shall be raised equally.

<u>Weight
adjustments following Declarations to Run</u>
Horses that are:
Deleted.
a reserve for the Race,

shall be
initially ignored for weight adjustments for any Handicap Flat Race:
After the deadline for Declarations to Run in a Handicap Flat Race, except for horses disregarded under paragraph 27, weights shall be adjusted in the following order:

the highest original weight, excluding penalties, of the horses that remain entered in the Race shall be raised by the lowest amount necessary to ensure compliance with either the weight maximum for older horses, or 9st 9lb, and the weight of all other horses raised equally, if:

the
weight of the highest weighted horse, excluding penalties, is less than the top

any penalty incurred after

the weight of any horse that remains below the bottom weight shall be raised to the bottom weight; and

9st 4lb, or

the minimum weight stated in

including weight adjustments

After the deadline for Declarations to Run in a Handicap Jump Race, except for horses disregarded under paragraph 33, weights shall be adjusted in the following order:

the highest original weight, excluding penalties, of the horses that remain entered in the Race shall be raised to the top weight, and the weight of all other horses raised equally, if the weight of the highest weighted horse, excluding penalties, is less than the top weight;

for an Early Closer, the weight of the highest
weighted horse ignoring penalties is less than the top weight; or

any penalty incurred after the date stated in the Race
Conditions shall be added to the weights, except that no penalty may increase a
horse's weight above 12st 9lb in any Race and no penalty may be added where the
original or final weight is equal to or above that weight;
the weight of any horse that remains below the bottom weight shall be raised to the bottom weight; and

for any Handicap Jump Race that is not confined to
Amateur Jockeys, if applicable the weight of the lowest weighted horse shall be
lowered, and the weights of all other horses lowered equally, to the higher of:
11st 2lb, or

the
minimum weight stated in the Race Conditions.
A penalty incurred after the deadline for Declarations to Run shall be calculated on the original weight:

including weight adjustments
under paragraphs 32, 34.1 and 36; and,

excluding any increase under
paragraph 34.3.

After any weight adjustments under paragraphs 34 to 35, the weight of any horse that was disregarded under paragraph 33 shall be adjusted by adding or removing the amount by which the weights of the other horses were raised or lowered.

If a weight adjustment under paragraph 36 causes the top weight (excluding penalties) to exceed 12st 9lb, the top weight will be lowered to a maximum of 12st 9lb and all other weights lowered accordingly.

sections.html:
Weight adjustments following a Scratching Deadline or Confirmation of Entry

After a Scratching Deadline or Confirmation of Entries for any Handicap Jump Race that is an Early Closer, the highest original weight of the horses that remain entered in the Race shall be raised to the top weight and all other entries shall be raised equally.

Weight adjustments following Declarations to Run

Horses that are:

Deleted;

a reserve for the Race;

Declared to Run and the Race is a Second Preference Race;

entered in a Class 1 Handicap Race and at the deadline for Declarations to Run:

have run in a Race within the immediately preceding 24 hours, or

are already Declared to Run in another Race which has not been abandoned,

shall be initially ignored for weight adjustments for any Handicap Jump Race.

After the deadline for Declarations to Run in a Handicap Jump Race, except for horses disregarded under paragraph 33, weights shall be adjusted in the following order:

the highest original weight, excluding penalties, of the horses that remain entered in the Race shall be raised to the top weight, and the weight of all other horses raised equally, if the weight of the highest weighted horse, excluding penalties, is less than the top weight;

for an Early Closer, the weight of the highest weighted horse ignoring penalties is less than the top weight; or

otherwise, the weight of the highest weighted horse is less than the top weight;

any penalty incurred after the date stated in the Race Conditions shall be added to the weights, except that no penalty may increase a horse's weight above 12st 9lb in any Race and no penalty may be added where the original or final weight is equal to or above that weight;

the weight of any horse that remains below the bottom weight shall be raised to the bottom weight; and

for any Handicap Jump Race that is not confined to Amateur Jockeys, if applicable the weight of the lowest weighted horse shall be lowered, and the weights of all other horses lowered equally, to the higher of:

11st 2lb, or

the minimum weight stated in the Race Conditions.

A penalty incurred after the deadline for Declarations to Run shall be calculated on the original weight:

including weight adjustments under paragraphs 32, 34.1 and 36; and,

excluding any increase under paragraph 34.3.

After any weight adjustments under paragraphs 34 to 35, the weight of any horse that was disregarded under paragraph 33 shall be adjusted by adding or removing the amount by which the weights of the other horses were raised or lowered.

If a weight adjustment under paragraph 36 causes the top weight (excluding penalties) to exceed 12st 9lb, the top weight will be lowered to a maximum of 12st 9lb and all other weights lowered accordingly.

sections.title: CATEGORY A PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES

nested.html: The substances set out at paragraphs 1 to 6 below are defined as Category A Prohibited Substances.
The following anabolic agents:
anabolic androgenic steroids;
other anabolic agents, including but not limited to selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs);
beta-2 agonists, unless the substance is prescribed by a veterinarian as a bronchodilator at the appropriate dose and does not exceed two courses of treatment within any six month period.
*See BHA Notice: Clenbuterol here
The following peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances (save where oxytocin is used in fillies and mares in breeding management or to block oestrus cycling):

erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, including but not limited to erythropoietin (EPO), epoetin alfa, epoetin beta, darbepoetin alfa, and methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta, peginesatide, hypoxia inducible factor (HIF)-1 stabilisers;
growth hormones and growth hormone releasing factors, insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), and other growth factors;
synthetic proteins and peptides and synthetic analogues of endogenous proteins and peptides not registered for medical or veterinary use.
The following hormone and metabolic modulators:
aromatase inhibitors;
selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMS) and other anti-estrogenic substances;
agents modifying myostatin function, including but not limited to myostatin inhibitors;
insulins;
peroxisome proliferator activated receptor δ (PPAR δ) agonists, including but not limited to GW 1516;
AMPK activators, including but not limited to AICAR (5-aminoimidazloe-4-carboxamide-1-β-D-ribofuranoside).
Threshold Substances

The concentration specified in relation to each of the following substances is the minimum concentration that must be present before a Sample is regarded as testing positive for the substance. The substances and the thresholds are:
Boldenone - 0.015 microgram fee and conjugated Boldenone per millilitre in urine from male horses (other than geldings)
Estranediol in male horses (other than geldings): 0.045 microgram free and glucuroconjugated 5α-estrane-3β, 17α - diol per millilitre in urine*
Methoxytyramine - 4 micrograms free and conjugated 3-methoxytyramine per millilitre in urine
Testosterone:

0.02 microgram free and conjugated testosterone per millilitre in urine from geldings when, at the screening stage, the free and conjugated testosterone exceeds five times the free and conjugated epi-testosterone, or
0.055 microgram free and conjugated testosterone per millilitre in urine from fillies and mares (unless in foal), or
100 picograms free testosterone per millilitre in plasma from geldings, fillies and mares (unless in foal)
NON-APPROVED SUBSTANCES
Other substances with a similar chemical structure or similar biological effect to those set out in paragraphs 1 to 4 above.

Any substance not addressed by any of the other classes of substances, and which has no current approval by any government regulatory authority for veterinary use, or any substance not universally recognised by veterinary regulatory authorities as valid veterinary therapeutic treatment.
*When, at the screening stage, the free and glucuroconjugated 5α-estrane-3β, 17α- diol exceeds the free and glucuroconjugated 5, 10-estrene-3β, 17α-diol in the urine
NB: The conjugated substance is the substance that can be liberated from conjugates.

sections.title: CATEGORY A PROHIBITED METHODS

nested.html: The methods set out at paragraphs 7 to 11 below are defined as Category A Prohibited Methods.
MANIPULATION OF BLOOD AND BLOOD COMPONENTS

Withdrawal, manipulation and re-infusion of homologous, heterologous or autologous blood, blood products or blood cells into the circulatory system, with the exception of those used for life-saving purposes or as veterinary regenerative therapies for the treatment of musculoskeletal injury or disease.
BLOOD TRANSFUSIONS
Giving a blood transfusion to a horse or allowing or causing a blood transfusion to be given for the purposes of enhancing its performance.
GENETIC AND CELLULAR MANIPULATION
Modification of the heritable genome at any time of a horse's life. Any gene therapy or cellular manipulation in a horse must not be capable of:
giving the horse an advantage or disadvantage in a race contrary to the horse's inherent merits; or
being detrimental to the horse's welfare

The BHA may, at its discretion, allow or disallow racing by horses or their offspring after such therapy. Any gene therapy for a horse intended to race must be fully documented in the horse's Passport or in such manner as required by the BHA and shall be reported immediately to the BHA.
OXYGEN CARRIERS
Products that artificially enhance the uptake, transport or delivery of oxygen, including, but not limited to:
perfluorochemicals;
efaproxiral (RSR13); and
modified haemoglobin products (excluding the use of licensed veterinary treatments in situations of acute, life-threatening anaemia).

sections.title: CATEGORY B PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES

nested.html: The substances set out at paragraphs 12 to 15 are defined as Category B Prohibited Substances.
Any substance that is capable at any time of causing an action and / or effect, within one or more of the following mammalian body systems:
nervous system;
cardiovascular system;
respiratory system;
digestive system;
urinary system;
reproductive system;
musculoskeletal system;
blood system
immune system (except for licensed vaccines against infectious agents);
endocrine system.
Endocrine secretions and their synthetic counterparts;
Masking agents.
THRESHOLD SUBSTANCES

The concentration specified in relation to each of the following substances is the minimum concentration that must be present before a Sample is regarded as testing positive for the substance. The substances and thresholds are:
Arsenic: 0.3 microgram total arsenic per millilitre in urine;
Arsenic: 0.015 microgram total arsenic per millilitre in plasma;
Available Carbon Dioxide: 36 millimoles per litre in plasma;
Cobalt: 0.1 micrograms (= 100 nanograms) total cobalt per millilitre in urine;
Cobalt: 0.025 micrograms (= 25 nanograms) total (free and protein bound) cobalt per millilitre in plasma;
Hydrocortisone: 1 microgram per millilitre in urine;
Prednisolone: 0.01 micrograms free prednisolone per millilitre in urine;
Salicylic Acid: 750 micrograms per millilitre in urine or 6.5 micrograms per millilitre in plasma.

whilst taking a Notifiable Medication if they consider that the Jockey will be
fit to do so; or
recommend to the Licensing Committee that the Jockey’s Licence be suspended until the course of medication is completed or the Jockey’s medical status is no longer a cause for concern.
