sections.title: SAMPLING OFF THE RACECOURSE

nested.html:
A Jockey must always be contactable using the contact details that they
have provided to the BHA.

If an Approved Person gives the Jockey notice by telephone, the Sample
must be taken as soon as possible and in any event within 8 hours of the first
contact. The Jockey shall nominate a suitable, private place that is easily
accessible to meet the Approved Person and provide the Sample. In the event
that the Approved Person deems the meeting place to be unsuitable, the Jockey
shall propose alternative(s).

The Jockey must bring identification and may be accompanied by one
other person.

sections.title: URINE SAMPLING ON THE RACECOURSE

nested.html:
Jockeys engaged to
ride shall be selected to provide a urine Sample as follows:

The Jockeys will be selected
randomly by a BHA Official in the presence of the Approved Person, save that:

any Jockey who is subject to the enhanced sampling programme
must be tested; and

the BHA may select further Jockeys for testing at its
discretion (if authorised by a BHA executive director).

Where a Jockey has
been selected to provide a urine Sample, they must:

sign to acknowledge that they
have been notified of the selection; and

provide a urine Sample as soon as reasonably
practicable, without leaving the Racecourse and in any event within 30 minutes
of the finishing time of the last Race of the Race Meeting.

A Steward may exempt
a Jockey from the requirement to provide a urine Sample in limited
circumstances, such as where the Jockey:

is unable to get to the Race Meeting where they are
required to provide the urine Sample; or

is engaged to ride at another Race Meeting taking place
later that day and it would be unreasonable to require them to provide the
urine Sample.

A Jockey shall not
be in breach of paragraph 10.2 where they can establish that:

there was a satisfactory explanation for failing to
provide a urine Sample: and

where they did not seek exemption from a Steward
pursuant to paragraph 11, there was a satisfactory explanation for failing to
seek such an exemption; or

where they did seek exemption from a Steward pursuant
to paragraph 11 but the exemption was refused, the exemption was refused
wrongfully.

The procedure
relating to the taking of a urine Sample shall be as follows:
The Jockey must report to the location assigned for sampling by the Approved Person.
The Jockey must select an unused plastic collecting vessel and must give the Sample in the presence of the Approved Person.

To ensure the authenticity of the Sample, the Approved Person may require exposure of the Jockey’s body from the middle of the back to below the knees. If the Approved Person has reason to believe that the Sample is not an authentic Sample, they may require a further Sample and both Samples will be sent to the laboratory.

If the volume of urine produced by the Jockey is 30ml or more, the Sample will be deemed complete and the process will continue from paragraph 13.9 below. If not, the process will continue from paragraph 13.5 below.
<u>Partial Sample</u>

The partial sample shall be stored in a temporary bottle and sealed in
the corresponding container. The unique ID number on the temporary bottle and
container shall be confirmed by the Jockey.

When the Jockey is ready to provide more urine, the process set out in paragraphs 13.3 to 13.4 and shall be repeated until a sample of 30ml or more has been provided. After each Sample is given, the Jockey will check the seal on the temporary container before the Approved Person breaks it and pours the additional urine from the collecting bottle into the temporary bottle. In the event that a Sample of 30ml or more is not provided within 30 minutes of the end of the last Race, this process shall stop and any partial Sample shall be destroyed.
A Jockey may leave before having produced a complete Sample, but must return to provide a complete Sample.
When the volume of urine produced by the Jockey reaches or exceeds 30ml, the process will continue from paragraph 13.9 below.
<u>Complete Sample</u>

The Jockey must choose a pair of unopened empty bottles from a standard
sampling control kit each of which shall bear unique ID numbers.
In the presence of the Approved Person, the Jockey and any accompanying person:

the bottles shall be sealed and the seal shall be
tested by the Jockey or the Approved Person by inverting the bottles;

the Jockey and the Approved Person shall check the
container seal and the unique ID number against that recorded; and

the Jockey shall inform the Approved Person of any drugs
or medications they have taken in the last seven days.

The Jockey and the Approved Person shall sign the chain of custody form and any accompanying person shall be invited to do likewise. Any irregularities in the Sample collection procedure to that point that are identified by the Jockey or any accompanying person shall be indicated on the chain of custody form before signature, otherwise the signature will certify that the Jockey is satisfied with the Sample collection procedure.
<u>Analysis of the urine Sample</u>

The sealed containers carrying the A Sample and the B Sample will be
placed in an outer transport bag, together with a sealed envelope labelled
‘Confidential’ containing the (white) laboratory copy of the chain of custody
form.
The yellow copy of the chain of custody form shall be placed in the stamped addressed envelope provided, sealed and labelled ‘Confidential’ and sent to the BHA immediately.
The Approved Person shall prepare a report that appends the race card and/or Jockey list and records:
the number of ‘A’ and ‘B’ Samples collected;
the selection procedure;

the details of any matters which might need to be brought
to the attention of the Chief Medical Adviser; and
the approved collecting agent relating to facilities.

The BHA shall inform the Approved Person how many urine tests are to be conducted in relation to each category of Jockey at a Race Meeting;

any Jockey who is subject to the enhanced sampling programme must be tested; and

is unable to get to the Race Meeting where they are required to provide the urine Sample; or

sections.title: ALCOHOL

nested.html:
At any Race
Meeting, the BHA may require a Jockey to undergo one or more breath tests for
alcohol at any time. Where the BHA does so, no Jockey may ride in a Race until
they have completed the test(s).
14A Exemption from testing will not normally be granted by the Stewards in respect of breath sampling
Breath testing for alcohol shall be carried out as follows:
A screening Sample will be taken and tested. If the result indicates that a breath test to obtain a quantitative reading is necessary, one shall be carried out immediately (the First Breath Sample).

If the First Breath Sample indicates the presence of alcohol at or above the limit specified in in the Rules, a second quantitative breath Sample shall be taken within 15 minutes of the First Breath Sample (the Second Breath Sample).

If the Second Breath Sample, after being subjected to a quantitative test, also indicates the presence of alcohol at or above the permitted limit, the Jockey will be immediately suspended from riding for the rest of that day and the matter shall be referred to the BHA.

sections.title: INTERIM SUSPENSION

nested.html: The BHA may immediately suspend a Jockey’s Licence pending a disciplinary hearing if a Jockey:
returns a Positive Analysis;
fails or refuses to give a Sample; or

Where an interim suspension is imposed:
The Jockey will be entitled to a disciplinary hearing on an expedited basis; and
other than in exceptional circumstances, the interim suspension will be credited against any penalty imposed by the Disciplinary Panel.

sections.title: AIMS OF THE BHA SAFEGUARDING FUNCTION

nested.html: The BHA is committed to ensuring the welfare of Young Persons and Adults at Risk within racing. The BHA expects all Persons to share this commitment and maintain appropriate standards and behaviour in their dealings with Young Persons and Adults at Risk.

These Safeguarding Rules, incorporating the NSP Rules, establish a procedural framework through which the BHA may investigate matters concerning the harm, or possibility of harm, to Young Persons and Adults at Risk, and through which such matters may be addressed and determined.

The core aim of these Safeguarding Rules is to ensure the safety and welfare of Young Persons and Adults at Risk. The procedures detailed in these Safeguarding Rules are intended to be fair, straightforward and tailored to the needs of racing.

sections.title: PROHIBITED CONDUCT AND THE PROTECTION OF YOUNG PERSONS AND ADULTS AT RISK

nested.html: No Person may;

list.html: engage, or attempt or threaten to engage, in conduct that directly or indirectly harms the physical and/or mental welfare and/or safety of one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk, and/or
pose a risk of harm to the physical and/or mental welfare and/or safety of one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk (‘Prohibited Conduct’).

nested.html: NOTE:

list.html: 'Harm' is not a narrow concept, and can mean different things in different contexts. Reference should be made to the BHA Safeguarding Policy.

It is not necessary for Prohibited Conduct to take place or arise in the context of racing and/or related activities. For example (and without limitation), in the event that a Person has been convicted or cautioned for, charged with, or arrested for any offence that concerns harm to one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk (whether or not those Young Persons or Adults at Risk participate in racing), that may form the basis of action under these Safeguarding Rules as a result of that Person posing (or potentially posing) a risk of harm (regardless of whether or not the relevant offence, or alleged offence, took place in the context of racing and/or related activities).

The BHA recognises that, as in many activities, sexual relationships can develop within the sport of horseracing. However, an adult in a position of trust – meaning where an adult (1) has contact with a Young Person or Adult at Risk, (2) has a role that carries an expectation of trust, and (3) is in a position to exercise authority, power or control over the Young Person or Adult at Risk (as perceived by the Young Person or Adult at Risk) – must not engage in inappropriate sexual activity with a Young Person or Adult at Risk who they employ, care for, etc. (including not grooming a Young Person or Adult at Risk for sexual activity when that person no longer qualifies as a Young Person or Adult at Risk). A sexual relationship between an adult in a position of trust and someone over whom the adult has (or had) a position of trust will often be a breach of trust and an abuse of the relevant adult’s position. Inappropriate sexual relationships may result in an investigation or proceedings under these Safeguarding Rules, whether or not the relationship results in the commission of a criminal offence.

sections.title: BHA SAFEGUARDING CASE MANAGEMENT GROUP

nested.html: The BHA shall establish a BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group that (once established) shall be responsible for reviewing and guiding/assisting the work of the BHA and the BHA’s wider safeguarding function in respect of case management pursuant to the Safeguarding Rules. The BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group shall comprise a minimum of three persons, each of whom shall be of suitable experience, and at least one of whom shall be independent of the BHA and have at least ten years’ safeguarding experience drawn from a relevant legal, investigative, social care, risk assessment, and/or offender management background.

The BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group shall meet (1) at least once every two calendar months in order to review and discuss the progress of all active safeguarding cases being handled by the BHA’s safeguarding team - being, at any one time, all cases from the point of considering investigation to the point of the conclusion of any case (including by way of any form of appeal or review proceedings), and (2) as and when requested by the BHA, e.g., to seek guidance/assistance on an urgent matter.

The BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group may recommend and advise actions to be taken by the BHA in respect of any case(s). However, the BHA will retain ultimate responsibility for decisions made in respect of the handling of cases arising under these Safeguarding Rules.

sections.title: THE BHA'S POWERS OF INVESTIGATION

nested.html: Upon the receipt of information from any source that gives the BHA reasonable ground(s) to suspect that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)), the BHA will be entitled to investigate the matter.
10.	In relation to any investigation commenced under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA may:
investigate the matter itself; and/or
appoint others, including an independent safeguarding expert (or experts), to assist the BHA in relation to its investigation or investigate the matter on the BHA’s behalf.

Section L of the Rules also applies to investigations undertaken pursuant to the Safeguarding Rules. The BHA may also require any Person (and request any other persons) to undertake a risk assessment by a suitably qualified person appointed by the BHA in such form as the BHA, at its discretion, considers appropriate (the cost of any such assessment in respect of a Person being risk assessed shall be borne by that Person, unless the BHA considers in the circumstances of an individual case that it is more appropriate for the cost to be borne by the BHA).
In carrying out investigations under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA will have special regard to and will always take account of:
the risk of harm that may be caused to Young Persons, Adults at Risk and others as a consequence of the investigation, particularly those who might already have been subject to harm; and
how to minimise that risk of harm, balanced against the need to ensure the proper conduct and effectiveness of the investigation.

sections.title: SUPPORTING PROVISIONS

nested.html: No Person may knowingly employ, engage or otherwise instruct any individual who, in undertaking the activities for which they are employed, engaged or instructed, poses a foreseeable risk of harm to Young Persons or Adults at Risk.

Without prejudice to any other obligations set out in the Rules or any other relevant BHA rules, regulations or procedures, Persons must comply with any BHA Disclosure and Barring Service Checks Policy (as may be in force from time to time, and whether as applicant or employee).
All Persons subject to investigation under these Safeguarding Rules, or who may otherwise be asked to assist with any such investigation, must co-operate with the investigation.

No Person may subject any other Person or other party to any detriment on the ground or belief that that Person or other party has reported a safeguarding concern to the BHA and/or assisted the BHA in any manner in relation to investigations or proceedings brought under these Safeguarding Rules.

All Persons must report to the BHA any circumstances of which they are aware that indicate that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)). A report should be made by the reporting Person using the reporting form made available by the BHA (on its website or otherwise) from time to time.
No Person may make a malicious safeguarding report to the BHA, or otherwise act in bad faith in relation to matters covered by these Safeguarding Rules.

If any Person breaches any of the above provisions of this section (paragraphs 13-18), the BHA may take action against him or her under the Rules of Racing or any other applicable rules or regulations of the BHA (whichever is most appropriate in the circumstances).
NOTE:

The BHA wants to be presented with any information, from any source, where there is reason to consider that any Person has presented or presents a risk of harm to one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk, so that appropriate action may be taken. In order for the BHA's work under the Safeguarding Rules to be effective, the co-operation of all Persons is necessary when requested by the BHA (or those acting on its behalf). The BHA may therefore view a failure to co-operate, or conduct designed at preventing or dissuading others from reporting concerns or co-operating, as a serious disciplinary matter.

In the absence of cogent evidence to the contrary, the BHA will operate on a working presumption that (1) all reports of possible Prohibited Conduct are made in good faith, and (2) all Persons act in good faith in relation to matters covered by these BHA Safeguarding Rules. However, the BHA will also view malicious reporting or acts of bad faith in relation to safeguarding matters seriously (e.g. where a false report is made to pursue a personal vendetta or false information is deliberately provided to an investigation).

sections.title: PROVISIONAL RISK MANAGEMENT ORDERS

nested.html: In the absence of cogent evidence to the contrary, the BHA will operate on a working presumption that (1) all reports of possible Prohibited Conduct are made in good faith, and (2) all Persons act in good faith in relation to matters covered by these BHA Safeguarding Rules. However, the BHA will also view malicious reporting or acts of bad faith in relation to safeguarding matters seriously (e.g. where a false report is made to pursue a personal vendetta or false information is deliberately provided to an investigation).
Apply to the Judicial Panel Chair for the imposition of a Provisional Risk Management Order; or

In the circumstances where (a) the Judicial Panel Chair is not available to determine an application made pursuant to paragraph 20.1 (or delegate such determination in accordance with paragraph 31), and (b) the immediate imposition of a Provisional Risk Management Order is deemed necessary by the BHA, impose a Provisional Risk Management Order directly on the Person; or

Agree the terms of a Provisional Risk Management Order to be imposed upon the Person with the consent of that Person. Any such terms will be evidenced in writing between the BHA and the Person (in a form as directed by the BHA) and once evidenced in writing will be deemed to be a Provisional Risk Management Order (despite no form of order being required from the Judicial Panel Chair).

The imposition of Provisional Risk Management Orders pursuant to paragraph 20.2 shall coincide with (or otherwise be followed as soon as possible by) an application by the BHA to the Judicial Panel Chair to ratify the Order at the earliest practicable opportunity.

A Provisional Risk Management Order imposed pursuant to paragraph 20.3 will not require ratification by the Judicial Panel Chair. If either party wishes to withdraw from the Order or amend the terms of the Order without the consent of the other party, an application should be made to the Judicial Panel Chair for the Order to be reviewed at the earliest possible opportunity. The terms of the Order previously agreed will remain in force until the matter can be reviewed.

A Provisional Risk Management Order may prohibit or otherwise restrict a Person from all or any specific racing and/or related activities under the jurisdiction of the BHA, on such terms and conditions as might be reasonable and proportionate to the circumstances of the case.

A Provisional Risk Management Order shall be imposed only in cases where, and to the extent that, it is reasonable and proportionate. Prior to imposing a Provisional Risk Management Order, the BHA (in liaison with the BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group unless impractical to do so) will consider the following factors:
whether any Young Person or Adult at Risk (or other person) is or may be at risk of harm;

the prospect of any charge(s) made (or that might be made) pursuant to these Safeguarding Rules being upheld (i.e., the stronger the merits of the charge(s), the stronger the justification for a Provisional Risk Management Order);

the seriousness of the alleged Prohibited Conduct (including the seriousness of the risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)), i.e., the more serious a case is, the stronger the justification for a Provisional Risk Management Order;
whether a Provisional Risk Management Order is necessary or desirable to allow the conduct of any investigation by the BHA, the police, or any other relevant authority to proceed unimpeded;
the opinion of any safeguarding expert (should the BHA choose to seek such an opinion);
the impact (or potential impact) that imposing a Provisional Risk Management Order might have on the Person who may be subject to the Order; and
any other circumstances that might be relevant to the individual case.
NOTE:

The purpose of a Provisional Risk Management Order is to manage any immediate risk whilst investigations, either by a third party (e.g. police or any relevant local authority) or the BHA are ongoing. The purpose is not to resolve any disputes of fact. For risk assessment purposes and the assessment of whether an Order is reasonable and proportionate, the risk should be taken at its highest, meaning the decision-maker should assume the allegations are capable of being proved and assess the risk on that basis.
Where the Judicial Panel Chair considers an application, an application for ratification or a review in accordance with paragraph 20:
where applicable, the relevant application, and any decision in respect of it, may be made with or without notice being given to the Person;

the procedure for determining the application shall be determined by the Judicial Panel Chair, as appropriate to the circumstances of the application (the procedure shall include, save in exceptional circumstances, seeking representations from the Person);

the Judicial Panel Chair may seek the opinion of an independent safeguarding expert in determining the application (the cost of which shall be borne by the BHA, subject to any later costs order of a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal);

the test that the Judicial Panel Chair shall apply when determining the application or review is whether the Provisional Risk Management Order sought or imposed by the BHA is reasonable and proportionate, giving consideration to the factors set out at paragraph 24:

25.4.1	if the Judicial Panel Chair is satisfied that the Provisional Risk Management Order sought or imposed is reasonable and proportionate, the Judicial Panel Chair shall (as the case may be) impose or ratify the Order; and

if the Judicial Panel Chair is not satisfied that the Provisional Risk Management Order sought or imposed is reasonable and proportionate, the Judicial Panel Chair may either (a) not impose or ratify the Order, or (b) impose a Provisional Risk Management Order on such alternative terms and conditions as they consider are reasonable and proportionate in the circumstances.
When a Provisional Risk Management Order is imposed, the BHA shall ensure that the Person upon whom the Provisional Risk Management Order is imposed is promptly notified of the following matters:
the reasons why the Provisional Risk Management Order has been imposed, unless the BHA decides for good reason otherwise;
the scope of the Provisional Risk Management Order, i.e., which racing and/or related activities the Person is subject to temporary measures in relation to (up to and including all such activities);
such other terms and conditions as have been imposed; and
the date upon which the Provisional Risk Management Order shall take effect (which may be immediate).

The BHA will undertake periodic reviews of Provisional Risk Management Orders imposed on a Person in liaison with the BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group, giving due consideration to the factors set out at paragraph 24. The relevant period will be determined by the BHA with reference to the particular circumstances of the case.

The BHA may at any time (i.e., following periodic review or otherwise) lift or seek to vary the terms of a Provisional Risk Management Order imposed on a Person, giving due consideration to the factors set out at paragraph 24.

A Person who is subject to a Provisional Risk Management Order may, for good cause shown, request permission to apply to lift or vary the terms of the Order from the Judicial Panel Chair. The procedure for determining any request and consequent application shall be determined by the Judicial Panel Chair, who may refer the matter to the NSP in respect of any case proceeding before the NSP. Any application shall only be successful if and insofar as the relevant Person demonstrates the Provisional Risk Management Order imposed is not reasonable and proportionate to the circumstances of their case

For the avoidance of doubt, (1) any steps taken by the BHA concerning Provisional Risk Management Orders shall not serve to preclude the jurisdiction of the NSP (rather than a BHA Panel) to proceed to hear the merits of the charge(s), should the BHA elect to pursue the matter through the procedures under the NSP Rules pursuant to paragraph 32, and (2) Rule 6 of the NSP Rules (Conduct of applications relating to Provisional Suspensions) shall not apply to any applications under these Safeguarding Rules save to the extent an NSP Tribunal may apply it to matters referred to the NSP pursuant to paragraph 29.

The Judicial Panel Chair may in respect of any current or future application made under paragraphs 20-29 delegate their relevant functions to a member of the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool, in which case the above references to the Judicial Panel Chair shall be read instead as references to the designated member of the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool.

sections.title: NOTICE OF CHARGE AND RESPONSE

nested.html: If, as the result of an investigation commenced under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA concludes that the Person has a case to answer, the BHA shall send a written notice of charge to that Person:
confirming that a charge is being issued against the Person under these Safeguarding Rules and that the matter may be referred for determination by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal;
referring to (and attaching) any and all supporting evidence, information and/or documentation that the BHA wishes to rely on;
setting out the risk management measure(s)/order(s) that the BHA considers appropriate if the charge is admitted or upheld; and
requiring the Person’s written response to the charge within 14 days (or, where circumstances so warrant, such shorter or longer period as may reasonably be specified by the BHA).
A charged Person must:
admit the charge and accept the proposed risk management measure(s) (which, absent further direction by the BHA, will constitute an agreement in accordance with paragraph 52); or
admit the charge but:
not accept the risk management measure(s) proposed by the BHA; and

provide a written response on the appropriate risk management order(s) and refer to (and attach) any supporting evidence, information and/or documentation which the charged Person wishes to rely on, including a written witness statement from any fact or expert witness upon which the charged Person wishes to rely; or
deny the charge (in whole or in part), and:
provide a written response setting out why the charge should not be upheld; and

refer to (and attach) any and all supporting evidence, information and/or documentation that the charged Person wishes to rely on, including a written witness statement from any fact or expert witness upon which the charged Person wishes to rely.

If a notice of charge is sent to a Person who was under the age of 18 years when the relevant Prohibited Conduct is alleged to have occurred or arisen, the BHA may send a copy of the notice of charge to the charged Person’s parent or carer.

Following receipt of the Person's response to a written notice of charge, or in the event no such response is received within the period requested pursuant to paragraph 32.4, the BHA may (in their absolute discretion) refer the matter for a hearing before either a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal to determine appropriate risk management orders (if any) in accordance with paragraph 47 of these Safeguarding Rules. For the avoidance of doubt, no Person may appeal or challenge any aspect of the BHA’s decision as to whether to refer a matter to a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal (including whether such a referral is appropriate or as to which body a referral is made).

sections.title: PROCEDURE BEFORE BHA PANELS AND NSP TRIBUNALS

nested.html: If, following a notice of charge and any response, the BHA refers a Person to either a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA shall prepare and send a written notice of referral in the name of the BHA to the Person, which shall contain at least the following information:
an outline of the process to be followed in relation to the referral; and
contact details for the BHA Panel or the NSP Tribunal (as appropriate).

The following matters arising under these Safeguarding Rules may be determined by the NSP and NSP Tribunals in accordance with the NSP Rules, as amended from time to time, which are deemed to be incorporated by reference to this paragraph:
any referral to the NSP by the BHA on the basis that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)); and
any other matter that the BHA may reasonably refer to the NSP for determination in accordance with the NSP Rules.

The BHA may, as an alternative to a reference to the NSP under paragraph 37, refer a charge that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b), to a BHA Panel for determination in accordance with relevant parts of the Judicial Panels Code as though the Person were charged with a breach of the Rules of Racing. The Chair of any BHA Panel in such cases may read in such changes to the Judicial Panels Code as might be required and may give such directions as they consider appropriate for the purpose of ensuring a fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings, with particular regard for the sensitive nature of safeguarding proceedings and the possibility (if appropriate) of adopting one or more of the ‘special measures’, as set out in the NSP Rules. Such ‘special measures’ may also be adopted in respect of the evidence of any witness where appropriate.

In the case of any conflict between these Safeguarding Rules and the Judicial Panels Code, the former shall take precedence. Without limitation, the following provisions of the Judicial Panels Code shall not apply to any matter referred to a BHA Panel under these Safeguarding Rules:
Paragraphs 23 and 24 (Hearings Conducted in the Presence of the Media). (Paragraph 66 of these Safeguarding Rules applies instead).
Paragraphs 33 to 42 (Commencement of Proceedings and Charge Response Form). (Paragraphs 32-35 of these Safeguarding Rules applies instead).
Paragraphs 43 to 48 (Plea Agreement). (Paragraphs 51-57 of these Safeguarding Rules applies instead).
Paragraph 55 (Appeals). (Paragraphs 43-46 of these Rules and the NSP Rules (as amended by Paragraphs 43-46) apply instead).
Part Four (Disciplinary Panels as an Appellate Body) and Part Six (Licensing Committee).

In the case of any conflict between these Safeguarding Rules and the NSP Rules that is not specifically provided for by these Safeguarding Rules, the NSP Rules shall take precedence in relation to matters proceeding before the NSP. Otherwise, these Safeguarding Rules shall take precedence.

sections.title: SUMMARY PROCEDURE

nested.html: Notwithstanding any of the other provisions of these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA may, having liaised with the BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group, impose any risk management measure(s) on a Person by way of executive decision (i.e., without prior referral to a BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal). The BHA will impose such risk management measures when, and to the extent that, they are considered reasonable and proportionate by the BHA to manage an obvious risk to one or more Young Persons and/or Adults at Risk in light of receipt of the following information (and whether before or after affording the Person concerned the right to address any identified concern(s)):
that the Person has been convicted of, or made the subject of a caution in respect of a criminal offence concerning a Child or Adult at Risk;
that the Person has been found liable in respect of any other form of offence (e.g., a disciplinary or regulatory offence) or civil action; and/or
is included or placed on any statutory barring lists.
The BHA shall ensure that the Person upon whom any one or more risk management measure has been imposed is promptly notified of the following matters:
the reasons why the risk management measure has been imposed, unless the BHA decides for good reason otherwise;
the scope of the risk management measure(s);
such other terms and conditions as have been imposed (including any date(s) at which the risk management measure(s) may be reviewed);
the date upon which the risk management measure(s) shall take effect (which may be immediate); and
the Person’s right to appeal the imposition of the risk management measure(s).

sections.title: APPEALS

nested.html: The following decisions may be appealed to an NSP Tribunal (acting as an NSP Appeal Tribunal):
a first instance decision of a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal issued pursuant to the procedure set out at paragraphs 36-40 of these Safeguarding Rules; and
the imposition of risk management measures imposed by the BHA pursuant to the summary procedure set out at paragraph 41-42 of these Safeguarding Rules;
each to be deemed a first instance decision for the purposes of the NSP Rules.
The NSP Rules will apply to all appeals, subject to (1) paragraphs 43-46, and (2) mutatis mutandis (i.e., with changes deemed to have been made as required to reflect the different context).
In respect of first instance decisions of a BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal, the grounds of appeal available to each of the Person and the BHA shall be that:
the reasons given by the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal are insufficient to support the decision reached;
there was insufficient material on which the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal could have made the decision in question;
the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal failed to hold a fair hearing;
the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal misconstrued, failed to apply or wrongly applied these Safeguarding Rules (or any other relevant rules or regulations);
the order or risk management measure is so disproportionate that no reasonable BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal could have decided upon it; and/or

there is evidence available for the appeal that was not available or obtainable at first instance but which, had it been available at first instance, would have caused the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal to reach a materially different decision.

Save (1) in cases of appeals against the imposition of risk management measures imposed by the BHA pursuant to the summary procedure, or (2) where an NSP Tribunal orders otherwise as a consequence of exceptional circumstances, an appeal shall not be de novo and shall instead be by way of review of materials considered at first instance and any such additional evidence, except that:
oral submissions will be permitted; and
oral evidence will only be permitted if permission to introduce new evidence has been granted.

there is evidence available for the appeal that was not available or obtainable at first instance but which, had it been available at first instance, would have caused the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal to reach a materially different decision.

Save (1) in cases of appeals against the imposition of risk management measures imposed by the BHA pursuant to the summary procedure, or (2) where an NSP Tribunal orders otherwise as a consequence of exceptional circumstances, an appeal shall not be de novo and shall instead be by way of review of materials considered at first instance and any such additional evidence, except that:

oral submissions will be permitted; and

oral evidence will only be permitted if permission to introduce new evidence has been granted.

sections.title: RISK MANAGEMENT ORDERS

nested.html: BHA Panels, the BHA acting under the Summary Procedure set out above, and NSP Tribunals may impose such risk management orders and/or risk management measures as they see fit. However, the BHA envisages that the following range of risk management orders are appropriate where, on the balance of probabilities, a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal concludes that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)):
guidance as to future conduct;
an order requiring the Person to undertake specified training/education;
a reprimand;
a warning as to future conduct;

an order requiring the Person to be monitored in specific matters and/or for a specified period of time (up to and including indefinitely) by a specified person or entity (which monitoring may be ordered to be at the Person’s cost);
the suspension of, withdrawal of, or the imposition of conditions on, any licences, permits and/or registrations held by the Person, either temporarily or permanently;

a period of suspension or disqualification for a specific period of time (up to and including indefinitely) from involvement in any racing and/or related activities under the jurisdiction of the BHA on such terms and conditions as considered appropriate; and/or
an order excluding the Person from any premises licensed by the BHA for a specific period of time (up to and including indefinitely).
In determining the appropriate management order(s), BHA Panels and NSP Tribunals may take into account:
the seriousness of the Prohibited Conduct and/or risk of harm;
the impact of any relevant conduct on any affected Young Person or Adult at Risk;
the context of the particular situation (including whether there is a pattern of inappropriate behaviour or misconduct and the age(s) and/or other circumstances of the persons involved);
whether the Prohibited Conduct in question was deliberate, reckless and/or negligent;
any continuing risk a Person may pose;
the enforceability of any risk management order in practical terms; and
any ‘aggravating’ or ‘mitigating’ factors that exist (in the opinion of the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal) in the context of the particular circumstances.
BHA Panels and NSP Tribunals may choose to suspend all or part of any risk management order it has imposed.

sections.title: PUBLICATION

nested.html: The BHA may publish and/or share details of risk management orders and risk management measures, including Provisional Risk Management Orders or any other interim measures, on a ‘need to know’ basis in such form and manner, and to such extent, as it deems necessary for the purposes of enforcement and/or compliance. The BHA may also take such administrative steps as it deems necessary or appropriate in order to give effect to risk management orders and risk management measures, including Provisional Risk Management Orders or any other interim measures imposed by the BHA, BHA Panels and NSP Tribunals (i.e., such risk management orders will not require any further act of ratification by any other body).

sections.title: CONCLUSION OF CASES OTHER THAN BY DETERMINATION BY A BHA PANEL OR NSP TRIBUNAL OR SUMMARY PROCEDURE

nested.html: If, at any stage prior to a referral under paragraph 36, the BHA concludes that (1) there is insufficient evidence to charge/proceed with a charge, and/or (2) a referral would not further the aims of these Safeguarding Rules, and/or (3) there is any other bona fide reason for the BHA not to refer the matter, then the BHA may take such other action as it considers appropriate in all the circumstances of the case. For example, without limitation, the BHA may inform a Person that they have no case to answer under these Safeguarding Rules, provide a Person with guidance as to their future conduct, or refer the matter to another body (where the BHA is satisfied that other body will deal with the matter effectively).

Notwithstanding any of the other provisions of these Safeguarding Rules, at any time prior to the commencement of deliberations by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal, it will be open to a Person to agree with the BHA on the appropriate risk management measure(s) (including in respect of Provisional Risk Management Orders or any other interim measures) to be imposed upon him/her in order to avoid the need for a determination by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal.

Any such discussions between the BHA and the relevant Person may take place on a “without prejudice” basis and in such manner that they will not delay or in any other way interfere with an investigation or any proceedings.

Any resulting agreement will be evidenced in writing between the BHA and the relevant Person (in a form as directed by the BHA) and set out the risk management measure(s) imposed on the relevant Person.

In reaching an agreement under paragraph 52 of these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA will have due regard to the range of risk management orders set out at paragraph 47 of these Safeguarding Rules, but it may agree any measure(s) appropriate to the case at hand.
If an agreement is reached, determination by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal will not be required.

A Person who agrees to resolve proceedings in accordance with paragraph 52 of these Safeguarding Rules will waive their right to appeal against or otherwise challenge any aspect of the agreed outcome.

sections.title: EXCEPTIONAL MATERIAL

nested.html: In considering any Provisional Risk Management Orders, or any charge, appeal or other matter brought pursuant to these Safeguarding Rules, the relevant decision-makers may not in the ordinary course of events consider any evidence provided by either the BHA or the relevant Person that the other party has not seen and had a reasonable opportunity to respond to. Exceptionally however, the BHA or the relevant Person may make an application for permission to submit evidence that has not been provided to the other party where the BHA or the relevant Person considers that such evidence should not be provided to the other party because revealing it (or the identity of, or anything which might reveal the identity of, any individual within such evidence) to the other party may (1) create a risk of harm to any person, and/or (2) be unlawful, and/or (3) prejudice an ongoing investigation (by the BHA, the police, or any other relevant authority). Applications under this paragraph should be lodged with the Judicial Panel Chair or (following a referral to the NSP) the NSP President as soon as possible.

Where either the BHA or the relevant Person makes an application for permission to submit exceptional material to any relevant decision-maker, the applicant party shall provide reasonable advance notice to the other party, unless the applicant party considers that such written notice itself may (1) create a risk of harm to any person, and/or (2) be unlawful, and/or (3) prejudice an ongoing investigation. Any reply from the other party must be provided alongside any application.

The Judicial Panel Chair or NSP President will appoint an appropriate person from the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool or the NSP to determine any application brought under paragraph58, and the appointed person shall otherwise have no involvement in the proceedings. The appointed person will issue such directions as they consider appropriate to determine the application, and they may allow or reject the application in whole or in part. In making their decision, the appointed person may seek the opinion of an independent expert.

If the appointed person allows the evidence to be submitted to the relevant decision- maker but withheld from the other party, the appointed person shall consider whether a redacted version of the evidence and/or a summary of the evidence should be provided to the other party as an alternative.

sections.title: MISCELLANEOUS

nested.html: These Safeguarding Rules are to be interpreted and applied by reference to their core aim of ensuring the safety and welfare of Young Persons and Adults at Risk. Such interpretation and application shall take precedence over any strict legal or technical interpretations that may otherwise be proposed. The BHA's Safeguarding Policy and any related documents that may be published by the BHA from time to time may be referred to as interpretative aids.

In the event that any incident or other matter occurs that is not provided for in these Safeguarding Rules (whether it relates to conduct, jurisdiction, investigation, procedure, sanction or otherwise), then the BHA, Judicial Panel Chair, BHA Panel Chair (following a referral to a BHA Panel), or (following a referral to the NSP) the NSP President or any appointed NSP Tribunal may take such action as considered appropriate in the circumstances, taking into account the specific circumstances of the individual case and the principles of natural justice and fairness.

Minor practical or technical points will not serve to invalidate the procedure or any decisions or findings made under these Safeguarding Rules, so long as the principles of natural justice and fairness are not infringed.

In the event that any matter or conduct falling under these Safeguarding Rules also falls under any other part(s) of the Rules of Racing or any other relevant BHA rules, regulations or procedures (as may from time to time be in force), or is subject to investigation by the police or other public authority (or analogous body, such as another sports governing body), or is subject to any other legal/regulatory/disciplinary process, then the BHA, Judicial Panel Chair, BHA Panel Chair (following a referral to a BHA Panel), or (following a referral to the NSP) the NSP President or any appointed NSP Tribunal, may at any point temporarily suspend the procedure under these Safeguarding Rules. For the avoidance of doubt, in the event that any matter or conduct falling under these Safeguarding Rules also falls under any other part(s) of the Rules of Racing or any other relevant BHA rules or regulations, the BHA expressly reserves its right to bring proceedings under those other rules or regulations (regardless of whether proceedings are also brought under these Safeguarding Rules).

Save to the extent that disclosure and/or publication is provided for in these Safeguarding Rules, or is otherwise in accordance with the law, all matters considered under these Safeguarding Rules, will, so far as practicable, be regarded as confidential.
These Safeguarding Rules are governed by English law.

If any part of these Safeguarding Rules (including the NSP Rules) is ruled to be invalid, unenforceable or illegal for any reason, that part will be deemed deleted, and the rest of these Safeguarding Rules will remain in full force and effect.
Neither the BHA, nor any person employed by or appointed to assist the BHA, will be liable to any party for any act or omission unless it is actuated by malice or bad faith

These Safeguarding Rules have an effective date of 1st January 2019. The substantive provisions of these Safeguarding Rules shall not apply retrospectively to matters arising before that date (but, for the avoidance of doubt, a Person may be considered to pose a risk of harm as a consequence of conduct or circumstances that took place prior to the effective date).

These Safeguarding Rules were last amended on 20 May 2026 with such amendments coming into effect on that date, save that proceedings pending as at that date shall continue to be governed by the Safeguarding Rules as in force at the time the proceedings were brought (unless the parties to the proceedings agree otherwise).
The BHA may further amend these Safeguarding Rules from time to time. Such amendments will come into effect on the date specified by the BHA.
